summary: Array deletion helper (scalar-deleting-destructor-shaped) over an object array. a2 is a flag word: bit 2 (a2 & 2) selects the array path, bit 0 (a2 & 1) selects whether the backing allocation is freed. On the array path the element count is read from the allocation header at this[-1]; the helper walks the elements in reverse (stride 52 dwords = 208 bytes each), calling the per-element destructor VTableInitCallChain on each, optionally frees the allocation base at this[-1] via FreeWrapper_7bcf, and returns the base pointer. On the non-array path it runs the destructor once on this and returns it.

local_names.a2: destructor flags: bit 1 (value 2) = array flag, bit 0 (value 1) = free flag
local_names.v3: element count read from the allocation header at this[-1]
local_names.v4: allocation base pointer = this - 1 (points at the count word)
local_names.v5: walk pointer over the element array, advanced in reverse by the 208-byte element stride
local_names.this: element-array base (this[-1] holds the element count)

operations.description: Dispatch on the array flag: when (a2 & 2) != 0 take the array-deletion path, otherwise run the single-element path.
Read the element count v3 = *(this - 1) from the allocation header immediately before the array.
Compute the allocation base v4 = (char *)(this - 1) and the starting walk pointer v5 = (char *)&this[52 * v3], i.e. one stride (52 dwords = 208 bytes) past the last element.
Guard the iteration on v6 = v3 - 1 >= 0; with an empty array (v3 == 0) the destructor loop is skipped entirely.
do-while loop over v3 iterations seeded from v7 = v6 + 1, walking the elements in reverse: v5 -= 208, destructor call, --v7 until v7 is zero.
Call the per-element destructor VTableInitCallChain(v5) for each element during the reverse walk.
Guard the free on the free flag: only when (a2 & 1) != 0.
Free the allocation via FreeWrapper_7bcf(v4), where v4 is the allocation base (this - 1).
Return v4, the allocation base pointer, on the array path.
Single-element path: run the destructor VTableInitCallChain(this) once on the object itself.
Single-element path free guard: when (a2 & 1) != 0, free the object via FreeWrapper_7bcf(this).
Return this on the single-element path.
